title: Vibhishana crosses
hook: Ravana's brother chooses the other side

segments.voice: Yesterday: Angada in Ravana's court, the young prince whose foot nobody could lift. Plant your foot.

A family dinner where everyone agrees about something that's wrong, heads nodding around the table, and one person who can't nod along. The story rewinds a little, to a scene Valmiki puts before the bridge. Inside Lanka, Ravana calls his council. Monkeys are gathering on the far shore. What should we do? One after another, his generals and ministers say: we'll crush them, great king. Then his younger brother stands up. Vibhishana. And he says the thing nobody in that golden room wants to hear.
screen: `THE ONLY ONE WHO SAYS IT.` → `RAVANA'S COUNCIL OF WAR.` → `HIS BROTHER STANDS UP.`

segments.voice: Give Sita back, Vibhishana tells his brother. Taking her was wrong, and it will destroy Lanka. Make peace with Rama. He says it once, carefully, then again. And Ravana explodes. He calls his brother a traitor and a disgrace to the family, and in some tellings, including Tulsidas's, kicks him in front of the whole court. So Vibhishana makes a choice people still argue about. He rises into the air with four companions, crosses the sea, and hovers above Rama's camp. I'm Ravana's brother, he calls down. I've left everything. I've come for refuge. The monkeys are sure it's a trick, and Sugriva says kill him. Rama says no. In Valmiki's telling, Rama says it's his vow: anyone who comes to him even once asking for shelter, saying I am yours, he will protect, from anything. Even, he adds, if it were Ravana himself. Then, before a single battle, on the beach, Rama has Vibhishana anointed as the future king of Lanka. The tradition holds him two ways. Devotees revere Vibhishana as a great devotee who chose dharma over family. And an old Hindi saying uses him the other way, roughly: the insider brings down Lanka. Traitor or conscience, the story makes you look at both. What it's clear about is this: he spoke first. He told the truth inside the room twice before he ever walked out of it. Leaving wasn't his first move. It was his last.
screen: `GIVE HER BACK, HE SAYS. TWICE.` · `RAVANA CALLS HIM A TRAITOR.` · `ANYONE WHO COMES FOR REFUGE.` · `CONSCIENCE, OR TRAITOR?`

segments.voice: Think of a room that was bad for you, a group chat, a friendship, a job, a habit of talking about people, and look, with no judgment, at whether you ever said the true thing inside it. Then think of a room you're in now that isn't right: what would it sound like to say the true thing once, calmly, and if nothing changed, where's the door?
Vibhishana crosses. Ravana's younger brother, who told the truth twice and then walked over to Rama's side.
Your line: walk across. Rama's door stayed open, even to Ravana's brother. Sixty days now.

howItsDone: Hindu tradition honors Vibhishana as a devotee of Rama and one of the long-lived ones of tradition, and Rama's promise of refuge to him is often recited as a verse of assurance; the Hindi proverb about 'the insider bringing down Lanka' shows the other way people remember him.

original.note: Sanskrit: Vibhishana, Ravana's younger brother, who crossed over to Rama.

trapdoor: what you thought: a traitor switches sides.
what it means: a brother tells the truth inside the room, is thrown out, and asks for refuge, and Rama takes him in.
what a scholar hears: Rama's vow of refuge to anyone who says 'I am yours' (Yuddha Kanda) became a key text for the idea of surrender to God.
recall: the steady hero coming apart in grief
a line in the dust: a limit not to cross

notes: Order: the script says Valmiki puts Vibhishana's crossing before the bridge. Confirm, and decide whether the outline should swap days 58–60.

Rama's vow of refuge (Yuddha Kanda, the 'sakrd eva prapannaya' verse, commonly cited as 18.33) is paraphrased, not quoted. Confirm reference. The trapdoor says it became a key text for surrender (prapatti), especially in Sri Vaishnava tradition; confirm the wording.
The kick is attributed to 'some tellings, including Tulsidas's'; confirm it's in Sundar Kand.
The Hindi proverb 'ghar ka bhedi Lanka dhaye' is rendered loosely as 'the insider brings down Lanka'; confirm.
The name's meaning ('terrifying') is from the root bhis; confirm.
